meaning:
φαῦλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX: Pro.22:8 (עֶוֶל) Pro.29:9 (אֱוִיל), etc. ;]
slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning (see LS, see word), in NT, as frequently in cl., always with distinct moral reference (see Ellic., Past. Epp., 203; Hort, Ja., 85; Tr., Syn., LXXxiv), worthless, bad: Jhn.3:20, Tit.2:8, Jas.3:16; opposite to ἀγαθός (which see), Jhn.5:29, Rom.9:11, 2Co.5:10.†
SYN.: see: ἄθεσμος (AS)

elsewhere.note: For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.
For being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him who calls,
For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ that each one may receive the things in the body according to what he has done, whether good or…
and soundness of speech that can’t be condemned, that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us.
For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.
